contract_md:
- **POST-1** Input consists of integers in the specified order, with exactly \(N\) coordinate pairs and \(Q\) query pairs. \(1 \le N,Q \le 200{,}000\), \(1 \le W \le N\), \(1 \le X_i \le W\), \(1 \le Y_i,T_j \le 10^9\), and \(1 \le A_j \le N\). Initial cells are distinct. Block IDs are the one-based indices of the coordinate pairs.
- **POST-2** Output has exactly \(Q\) lines in query order. Each line contains one case-sensitive token, `Yes` or `No`. Repeated queries require repeated answers.
- **POST-3** At each integer time, remove the entire bottom row if it is full at the start of that time step. Then visit the surviving blocks from bottom to top. Each block stays if it is on the bottom row or the cell directly below is occupied at its visit. Otherwise it moves down one cell. A row that becomes full during movement can first be removed at the next integer time. A query at \(T_j+0.5\) returns `Yes` exactly when its block survives the step at \(T_j\).
- **POST-4** A removed block stays absent. A block at initial height \(Y_i\) survives every step \(T<Y_i\). At time \(1.5\), exactly the blocks in an initially full bottom row are absent. If any column is initially empty, all blocks survive all queries. These rules also apply when \(W=1\).
- **POST-5** Reflecting the columns or consistently renumbering blocks and query targets preserves the answer sequence. Raising every block by the same nonnegative integer and shifting every query time forward by that integer also preserves the answer sequence whenever both inputs satisfy the bounds.
- **POST-6** The program must handle the full input limits, including times up to \(10^9\). The limits require avoiding work proportional to the largest query time and quadratic workloads in the number of blocks or queries.
